report_name: New Ransomware Group 'Inception' Claims 1TB Data Theft from Verisk

threat_actors.name: Inception
threat_actors.description: A newly emerged ransomware group that claimed responsibility for a major cyberattack against Verisk on November 26, 2026. The group operates a double-extortion model, focusing on data theft and threatening public release to pressure victims.
threat_actors.goals: To extort a ransom payment from Verisk by threatening to release 1.01 TB of exfiltrated sensitive data.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
attack_patterns.description: The Inception group claimed to have exfiltrated 1.01 TB of sensitive data, including client insurance contracts and database records, from Verisk's network to their own servers.

attack_patterns.name: Data Staged
attack_patterns.description: The Inception group likely collected and staged 1.01 TB of targeted data from Verisk's network prior to exfiltration.

attack_patterns.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
attack_patterns.description: As a ransomware group, Inception's modus operandi includes deploying ransomware to encrypt victim systems, disrupting operations and adding pressure for payment as part of their double-extortion strategy.

attack_patterns.name: Inhibit System Recovery
attack_patterns.description: The threat actor likely uses commands such as 'vssadmin delete shadows' to delete volume shadow copies, hindering system recovery from backups.

malware.name: Inception Ransomware
malware.description: The ransomware associated with the Inception group, presumably used to encrypt victim systems as the final stage of their double-extortion attacks.

tools.name: vssadmin
tools.description: Suggested as a tool used by the ransomware to delete volume shadow copies with the command 'vssadmin delete shadows' to inhibit system recovery.

identities.name: Verisk
identities.description: A major American data analytics and risk assessment firm targeted by the Inception ransomware group. The group claimed to have stolen 1.01 TB of data, including proprietary models and client contracts.

identities.name: Victoria's Secret
identities.description: Mentioned as a client of Verisk whose insurance contract data was allegedly included in the 1.01 TB of exfiltrated data.

identities.name: Marsh
identities.description: A global professional services firm mentioned as a client of Verisk whose insurance contract data was allegedly included in the exfiltrated data.

identities.name: AON
identities.description: A global professional services firm mentioned as a client of Verisk whose insurance contract data was allegedly included in the exfiltrated data.

identities.name: USAA
identities.description: A financial services company whose de-identified location data for 6.91 million customers was allegedly exfiltrated from Verisk.

infrastructure.name: Inception Leak Site
infrastructure.description: The dark web leak site where the Inception group posted its claim of attacking Verisk and threatened to release the stolen data.

indicators.name: VSSAdmin Shadow Copy Deletion
indicators.pattern:
title: VSSAdmin Shadow Copy Deletion
id: 2b3c4d5e-6f7a-4b0c-8def-0123456789ab
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of vssadmin.exe to delete volume shadow copies, a common ransomware precursor activity to inhibit system recovery.
references:
  - https://www.ransomware.live/id/VmVyaXNrQEluY2VwdGlvbg
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-26
tags:
  - attack.t1490
  - attack.impact
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\vssadmin.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'delete'
      - 'shadows'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the execution of 'vssadmin' to delete volume shadow copies, a technique used by ransomware to prevent easy recovery.

indicators.name: Suspicious Data Transfer Tool Execution
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: Suspicious Data Transfer Tool Execution
id: 3c4d5e6f-7a8b-4c0d-9eff-1234567890bc
status: experimental
description: Detects the execution of legitimate data transfer tools like rclone.exe or megacopy.exe, which are commonly abused by ransomware groups for data exfiltration.
references:
  - https://www.ransomware.live/id/VmVyaXNrQEluY2VwdGlvbg
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-26
tags:
  - attack.t1041
  - attack.exfiltration
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\rclone.exe'
      - '\megacopy.exe'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the use of legitimate data transfer tools like rclone or megacopy, which are often abused by attackers for data exfiltration.

indicators.name: Large Scale Data Egress Monitoring
indicators.pattern:
title: Large Scale Data Egress
id: 4d5e6f7a-8b9c-4d0e-ae00-2345678901cd
status: experimental
description: Detects large, sustained outbound data transfers, which can be an indicator of data exfiltration prior to a ransomware attack.
references:
  - https://www.ransomware.live/id/VmVyaXNrQEluY2VwdGlvbg
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-26
tags:
  - attack.t1041
  - attack.exfiltration
level: medium
logsource:
  category: firewall
detection:
  selection:
    action: 'allow'
    sent_bytes|gt: 100000000 # 100 MB
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Monitors for large, sustained outbound data transfers to unknown destinations, a key indicator of data exfiltration.
